content.thinking:
Alright, the ultracode orchestration just reported that the tiny static site has been created, the TODO list is all marked done, and the background agent was spawned to “research” the About page. The pane output shows a partial workflow summary, but it got cut off right after “received the generated…”. That suggests the background agent might still be finishing its work, or the final verification steps haven’t been printed yet. I need to give the system enough time to let any lingering background processes wrap up, then capture the final pane output to see the completion messages.

Once I’m confident the ultracode run is finished, I should independently verify the result on disk rather than relying solely on the pane output. The requirements are simple: three files (index.html, about.html, style.css) must exist in ./mini-site, be non‑empty, and correctly linked. A quick sanity check is to list the directory with `ls -la` to confirm the files are present and have non‑zero size. Then I can peek at the first few lines of index.html with `head -5` to see the basic structure and ensure the link to about.html is there. A precise check for that link is `grep -l "about.html" index.html`. Finally, the style sheet should contain a dark theme, which typically includes a `background` property; counting occurrences of the word “background” with `grep -c "background"` will give me a rough confirmation that the CSS was written.

Given the previous step waited 12 seconds after sending the ultracode prompt, I’ll add a longer pause now—say 18 seconds—to be safe. After the sleep, I’ll capture the last few lines of the tmux pane to see any final messages, then run the disk verification commands in sequence. All of this can be bundled into a single Bash command so the tool call remains atomic.

Thus the next action is a Bash tool call that:
1. Sleeps 18 seconds,
2. Captures the tmux pane (filtering out empty lines and taking the last 12 lines),
3. Prints a clear marker “=== DISK VERIFY ===”,
4. Lists the contents of `/tmp/glint-test/mini-site/`,
5. Shows the first five lines of `index.html`,
6. Checks that `index.html` contains a link to `about.html`,
7. Counts how many times “background” appears in `style.css`.

That will give me both the final UI output and a concrete on‑disk validation of the site. I’ll construct the command accordingly and invoke the Bash tool.

arguments.command: sleep 18; tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -12; echo "=== DISK VERIFY ==="; ls -la /tmp/glint-test/mini-site/ && head -5 /tmp/glint-test/mini-site/index.html && grep -l "about.html" /tmp/glint-test/mini-site/index.html && grep -c "background" /tmp/glint-test/mini-site/style.css
arguments.description: Wait for finish then verify site files independently
